Package com.egradx.notification.template

Class EgradxNotificationType

java.lang.Object
com.egradx.notification.template.EgradxNotificationType
public final class EgradxNotificationType extends Object
One kind of message an application sends — order.shipped, password.reset — and the variables its templates may use. Declare one as a bean for each key: 

 @Bean
 EgradxNotificationType orderShipped() {
     return EgradxNotificationType.builder("order.shipped")
             .description("Sent to the customer when an order leaves the warehouse")
             .requires("customerName", "orderNumber")
             .optional("trackingUrl")
             .build();
 }

This declaration is the contract that makes rendering strict. ikon-v9 had none, so a caller who misspelt a variable got a message with a blank where the value should have been, and nobody found out until a customer did. Here:

  • a required variable missing from the model, or null, is refused;
  • an optional variable may be left out, and renders as empty;
  • a model entry that is neither is refused — it is almost always a misspelling of one that is;
  • a template that uses a variable the type does not declare is refused when it is loaded or saved, not when a customer is waiting for it.

No channel appears here. Which channel a message goes out on is the caller's decision, made at each call; a type only says what the message can contain.

      public boolean userCanOptOut()
      Whether people may opt out of this kind of message. When true, every send of it skips users whose preferences decline it on that channel; when false — the default — preferences are never consulted, which is what a password reset or an order confirmation must be.
